scope: Keep workspace controls usable when browser storage is denied or full, and accurately distinguish session-only state from durable local persistence.

source_control.push: Normal fast-forward push; remote branch ref verified at the exact runtime commit.

finding.reproduction: When setItem throws SecurityError or QuotaExceededError, layout, dock order, theme and density changes are still applied to the current editor page, but their UI status incorrectly said the change had been saved on the device. Undo and Redo had no persistence-failure context either.
finding.fix: All workspace appearance, layout, dock-order, profile load/delete/reset and Undo/Redo operations now use the boolean result of the guarded storage write. They retain session-local usability and clearly explain when browser storage prevents durable persistence.
finding.regression_test: A real Chromium test blocks writes to the workspace-preferences key, changes theme/layout/dock order, then runs Undo/Redo. It verifies current-session rendering, explicit non-durable wording, no stored preference, and zero page Save/Publish API writes.
preserved_contracts: workspace settings remain separate from Page Model
blocked storage does not crash the editor
localStorage remains the only workspace preference store

implementation.reuse_review: Reused the existing guarded localStorage adapter, workspace settings status region, workspace Undo/Redo, project-owned shell and Chromium fixture. No external source or dependency was needed for this focused persistence-state improvement.
